 Medium

 Print Jaipur: Rajasthan High Court Monday issued notices to the producer of the upcoming film “Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak” and other respondents, and directed that no videos, clips, trailers or promotional material related to the film be uploaded on any social media platform, including YouTube, without certification from Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC). A single-judge bench of Justice Sameer Jain passed the order while hearing a petition filed by Indian Medical Association (IMA), Rajasthan. The matter is listed next on Nov 20, the film’s scheduled release date. IMA, represented by advocates Priyanshi Katta and Pranjul Chopra, alleged that the film contains derogatory portrayals of doctors and the medical profession that could undermine the doctor-patient relationship and erode public trust. The association objected in particular to a dialogue suggesting that doctors write commission slips instead of prescriptions, arguing that it depicts doctors as driven by commissions rather than professional ethics and could reinforce hostility towards healthcare workers.  IMA said it was not seeking to curb creative freedom, but to protect the dignity of the medical profession, doctor-patient trust and the safety of healthcare workers. The court was informed that the film has not received CBFC certification. Additional Solicitor General Bharat Vyas, appearing for CBFC, submitted that the film would be examined through the prescribed scrutiny process. The court directed that no promotional material related to the film be uploaded or released on social media without the requisite certification under Section 5B of the Cinematograph Act, 1952, and asked CBFC to consider IMA’s representations and objections while examining the film.
